note: Our mapping of our framework text onto SCF identifiers. provenance=ai, confidence<1.0 — label it in the UI.

mappings.rationale: sabic_cybertrust.json 1.1 requires a management-approved information security policy communicated to staff and external parties — the exact wording of 5.1.
sabic_cybertrust.json 1.2 assigns security roles with a designated accountable individual holding authority — 5.2 roles and responsibilities plus 5.4 management responsibilities.
sabic_cybertrust.json 1.3 requires role-relevant awareness training on hire and annually thereafter — 6.3 awareness, education and training.

sabic_cybertrust.json 1.4 is an annual/change-triggered risk assessment; ISO 27002:2022 has no risk-assessment control, this obligation belongs to ISO 27001 clause 6.1.2, so an honest gap beats a forced mapping.
sabic_cybertrust.json 2.1 requires an inventory of hardware, software and data assets with assigned owners — 5.9 inventory of information and other associated assets.
sabic_cybertrust.json 2.2 requires classifying AND labelling SABIC information with per-level handling procedures — 5.12 classification and 5.13 labelling.
sabic_cybertrust.json 2.3 governs removable media handling — encryption, tracking and secure disposal — which is the full lifecycle scope of 7.10 storage media.
sabic_cybertrust.json 3.1 requires a least-privilege, business-need access policy with regular review — 5.15 access control rules and 8.3 information access restriction.
sabic_cybertrust.json 3.2 requires strong authentication with MFA for remote and privileged users — 8.5 secure authentication, 5.17 authentication information handling.
sabic_cybertrust.json 3.3 requires privileged accounts inventoried, tightly controlled and their activity monitored — the definition of 8.2 privileged access rights.
sabic_cybertrust.json 3.4 requires access revocation within 24 hours of leaving or changing role — 5.18 removal/adjustment of access rights, 6.5 post-termination obligations.
sabic_cybertrust.json 4.1 prescribes approved algorithms (AES-256, TLS 1.2+) for data at rest and in transit — the cryptography-use rules of 8.24.
sabic_cybertrust.json 4.2 covers key generation, distribution, storage, rotation and destruction — the key management lifecycle explicitly inside 8.24.
sabic_cybertrust.json 5.1 restricts facility access to authorised personnel with entry/exit logging — 7.2 physical entry controls, protecting the perimeter defined in 7.1.
sabic_cybertrust.json 5.2 names theft, fire, flood and power disruption — 7.5 protection against physical and environmental threats, with power covered by 7.11 supporting utilities.
sabic_cybertrust.json 5.3 requires equipment media to be wiped or physically destroyed with destruction certificates — 7.14 secure disposal or re-use of equipment, 7.10 for the media itself.
sabic_cybertrust.json 6.1 requires changes documented, tested and approved before implementation — the change-management control 8.32.
sabic_cybertrust.json 6.2 requires current anti-malware configured for real-time protection — directly 8.7 protection against malware.
sabic_cybertrust.json 6.3 requires regular, securely stored, restore-tested backups — the exact scope of 8.13 information backup.
sabic_cybertrust.json 6.4 requires regular scanning and remediation within defined timeframes — 8.8 management of technical vulnerabilities.
sabic_cybertrust.json 6.5 requires protected, retained security event logs that are reviewed for anomalies — 8.15 logging and 8.16 monitoring activities.
sabic_cybertrust.json 7.1 isolates SABIC-data systems from untrusted networks (8.22 segregation of networks) using firewalls and boundary access controls (8.20 networks security).
sabic_cybertrust.json 7.2 requires secure protocols (SFTP, HTTPS) for exchanging SABIC information over untrusted networks — 5.14 information transfer rules realised through 8.24 cryptography.
sabic_cybertrust.json 7.3 requires VPN-or-equivalent encrypted remote access with MFA — 6.7 remote working security measures plus the MFA requirement of 8.5.

sabic_cybertrust.json 7.4 mixes encrypted messaging of sensitive information (5.14 covers electronic messaging transfer) with spam and phishing filtering, which ISO 27002 treats under 8.7 malware protection.
sabic_cybertrust.json 8.1 requires an incident response plan defining roles, procedures and communication protocols — 5.24 incident management planning and preparation.

sabic_cybertrust.json 8.2 sets 24-hour notification to SABIC with impact and containment details — 6.8 timely event reporting and the 5.24 communication protocol, though the customer-specific deadline is contractual.
sabic_cybertrust.json 8.3 requires retained incident records (timeline, actions) — 5.28 collection and retention of incident evidence — including lessons learned, which is 5.27.
sabic_cybertrust.json 9.1 requires documented and tested continuity of SABIC-related services — 5.29 information security during disruption, with 5.30 for the ICT readiness half.
sabic_cybertrust.json 9.2 requires DR capability with defined and tested RTO/RPO — 5.30 ICT readiness for business continuity, supported by 8.14 redundancy of processing facilities.
sabic_cybertrust.json 10.1 requires regular self-assessment against the CyberTrust rules with remediation plans — 5.36 compliance with policies, rules and standards.
sabic_cybertrust.json 10.2 requires identifying and monitoring applicable legal and data-protection requirements — 5.31 legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements.

sabic_cybertrust.json 10.3 obliges supporting customer-run security audits with access to facilities, systems and documentation — 5.35 independent review of information security, with 8.34 governing how those audit accesses are controlled.
sabic_cybertrust.json 10.4 requires CyberTrust obligations to be contractually imposed on subcontractors and verified — 5.20 supplier agreements and 5.22 monitoring and review of supplier services.
sabic_cybertrust.json 10.5 drives improvement from incident analysis (5.27) and audits/assessments (5.35); ISO 27002 has no standalone continual-improvement control, that sits in ISO 27001 clause 10.
